  MONDAY, SEPTEMBER 14, 2020 AT 7:00 P.M.

The City of San Marino appreciates your attendance. Community interest provides the Public
Safety Commission with valuable information regarding issues of the community.

Regular Meetings are held on the 1st Monday of every month.

In compliance with the American Disabilities Act, any person with a disability who requires a
modification or accommodation in order to participate in a meeting should contact the
Administration Department at (626) 300-0700 at least 48 hours prior to the meeting.

  PURSUANT TO EXECUTIVE ORDERS N-33-20 AND N-29-20

In accordance with the Governor’s Executive Orders N-33-20 and N-29-20, and given the health
risk associated with COVID-19, this public hearing will be conducted via teleconference/virtual
meeting, without a physical location from which members of the public may attend. Members
of the public may access the meeting electronically via the zoom.us teleconference module
(Computer for Video Streaming).

Members of the public may observe and offer comment at this meeting telephonically or
otherwise electronically:

  1) Public comment will be accepted by email to fire@cityofsanmarino.org before or during
  the meeting, prior to the close of public comment on an item, to be read by the
  Committee during public comment. Lengthy public comment may be summarized in the
  interest of time.

  2) Public comment will also be accepted electronically via the zoom.us teleconference
  module.

If you are an individual with a disability and need a reasonable modification or accommodation
pursuant to the Americans with Disabilities Act (“ADA”) please contact the City Clerk via email

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

ROLL CALL:  Chair Hunter Chang, Vice Chair Jeff Boozell, Commissioner Eugene

  Alternate Zillah Tobiano

POSTING OF AGENDA
The agenda is posted 72 hours prior to each meeting at the following locations: City Hall, 2200
Huntington Drive, the Crowell Public Library, 1890 Huntington Drive and the Recreation
Department, 1560 Pasqualito Drive. The agenda is also posted on the City’s Website:
http://www.cityofsanmarino.org

WRITTEN COMMUNICATIONS OR PUBLIC WRITINGS DISTRIBUTED
All public writings distributed by the City of San Marino to at least a majority of the Public Safety
Commission regarding any item on this agenda will be made available at the Public Counter at
City Hall located at 2200 Huntington Drive, San Marino, California 91108.

PUBLIC COMMENTS
Section 54954.3 of the Brown Act provides an opportunity for members of the public to address
the Public Safety Commission on any item of interest to the public, before or during the
Commission’s consideration of the item, that is within the subject matter jurisdiction of the Public
Safety Commission.

COMMISSIONER REPORTS

meetings or conferences they may have attended.

BY:  Police Chief John N. Incontro

DATE:  September 14, 2020
SUBJECT:  POLICE DEPARTMENT UPDATE REPORT JULY AND
  AUGUST 2020

BACKGROUND

Each month the Police Department provides a brief update on crime, traffic issues, and other
items of interest to the public and to the Public Safety Committee.

DISCUSSION

This report will provide the Public Safety Commission with information for the months of July
and August 2020. The Pandemic has resulted in the continued altering of police services in our
community. We have had to forgo community engagement, neighborhood watch programs and
limited our contact with others in order to lessen the potential of infection. The services at the
front desk have been curtailed, limiting one on one contact other than emergencies or
reporting of serious crimes. The department is reviewing software programs that will enable
members of the public to utilize online reporting of minor crimes and lost items. This will
allow victims to stay safely at home and report these minor incidents.

This year Police Departments nationwide were faced with unprecedented times, beginning with
an ongoing pandemic and followed by civil unrest as a result of the events in Minneapolis. Police
Departments in California challenged over 24 police reform legislations, which would a
significant impact on how Police Officers conduct their duties in a negative manner. A majority
of the bills which would have a negative impact were defeated. Bills that are currently pending
the Governor’s signature, do not impact the department, as is.

As of August 31, 2020, Part 1 crimes have increased 38.46%, this year compared to last year to
date. We continue to see the increases in commercial burglaries and larcenies. A further
examination of those two types of crimes has shown a decrease from 28 larcenies in May to 12
this month and four commercial burglaries in May to only one in June.

  2-1  AGENDA ITEM 2
 Throughout July and August 2020, the 27 larcenies have been primarily package thefts or
vehicle thefts of unlocked vehicles. The city suffered seven residential burglaries, one of which
occurred in a vacant home, two occurred in homes currently under construction. No alarm,
but there were surveillance cameras. One where the victim found the suspect standing inside
the threshold of the French door to the backyard. The suspect fled the scene prior to the
officers’ arrival.

INVESTIGATIVE FOLLOW-UP

The following is a description of activates completed by Detective personnel during July and
August 2020; Detective Bureau completed the following activates;
   The Detective Bureau filed 18 and 15 cases for prosecution with the Alhambra District
  Attorney’s Office, respectively.
   The San Marino Police Department engaged with the San Marino Chinese Club and the
  San Marino School District, regarding a potential hate crime. The San Marino Police
  Department has determined that the hate crime is unfounded.

COMMUNITY ENGAGEMENT

With the continued COVID-19 concerns the department has not engaged in community
engagement.

PERSONNEL UPDATE

The department currently has 27 of the 30 sworn positions filled. We are continuing to fill the
additional three positions, one is a lateral candidate who started with the department on
September 6, 2020, another is a lateral who is currently in the background investigation
process, one who has completed the background investigation face, and one who is beginning
the background investigation phase. We have one vacancy for Dispatcher and three for Cadet.

TECHNOLOGY

The department now has 22 Flock Safety cameras installed throughout the City. Specific
personnel have received access to the system and others will receive an orientation that will
provide them with the ability to work with the system and obtain information or evidence. The
Flock Safety cameras have assisted in two separate incidents, where two stolen vehicles were
recovered.

TRAFFIC REPORT

With the approval of the Fiscal Year 20/21 Budget, the Capital Equipment Plan and our Traffic
Safety Priority Initiative we will begin to move forward in reducing injury traffic collisions
through, education, enforcement and community involvement.
  2

  2-2  AGENDA ITEM 2
 Traffic enforcement is based upon three areas; traffic complaints from the community,
observation of violations by officers, and traffic collision data. The Department maintains a list
of traffic complaint locations and traffic collision data for traffic enforcement. As part of our
traffic collision investigations we will look for other issues that may have been a contributory
factor in the collision. Those factors could be distracted driving, engineering, or environmental.
The traffic data utilized for traffic enforcement are the top five locations for traffic collisions and
the top Primary Collision Factors (PCF’s), or causes of the traffic collisions. That information is
in the following chart.

FROM:  M. D. Rueda, Fire Chief

DATE:  September 14, 2020

SUBJECT:  FIRE DEPARTMENT UPDATE REPORT

BACKGROUND

The San Marino Fire Department is dedicated to providing the highest level of service to the
residents and visitors of the City of San Marino. As such, each month the San Marino Fire
Department provides an update on Department events and performance metrics to the public
and to the Public Safety Commission.

MONTHLY PERFORMANCE METRICS

Since the last Public Safety Commission Meeting, the Fire Department has submitted the July
Monthly Performance Metrics to the City Council. A copy of the July report has been included
in this update. The report includes the number of responses made by the Department, training
hours, Fire Prevention inspections, and the Department’s cardiac arrest performance for the
month of June.

CORONAVIRUS (COVID-19) RESPONSE

The Fire Department continues to maintain responsibility for the implementation of the elements
of the City’s Disease Pandemic Annex of the Emergency Operations Plan. The primary missions
include crisis communications to the public, resident support through the hotline, and the
operation of the City’s Emergency Operations Center (EOC).

The Fire Department has also initiated a Recovery Leadership Team meeting to ensure the City
is prepared as circumstances involving the pandemic change. Policies, procedures, physical
enhancements for opening City facilities to the public have been completed, however, all City
facilities remain closed until September 30, 2020.

  3-1  AGENDA ITEM 3
 The Fire Department has established policies and procedures for the daily and weekly sanitization
of the Fire Department quarters, apparatus, and PPE during the COVID-19 response.

PERSONNEL

The San Marino Fire Department celebrated the retirement of Firefighter/Paramedic Russ Wilcox
on Saturday, August 8. Firefighter Wilcox was a firefighter with the City of San Marino for 23
years. Following Firefighter Wilcox’s retirement, the Fire Department began the process of
conducting interviews to fill the vacated position. The department has currently placed four
candidates into the background evaluation process.

TRAINING

San Marino Fire Department personnel have continued to train, adapt, and prepare to serve our
residents during these extraordinary circumstances. During the month of August, Fire
Department personnel participated in 373 hours of training. Training included injury and illness
prevention, continuing EMS education with the UCLA Nurse Educator, HAZMAT management,
hose lays and ladders, commercial building construction, and officer training. Probationary
firefighter training continued for the department’s three probationary firefighters.

The month of August also presents the opportunity for the Fire Department to complete our
wild-land training preparations. The Fire Department conducts extensive training in preparation
for our wild-land season. Realistically, for the past several years the wild-land season has been
year round.

SIGNIFICANT INCIDENTS

On Monday, August 3 Firefighter/Paramedic Brian Campbell was assigned as a Fireline
Paramedic to the Apple Fire in the San Bernardino National Forest. Firefighter Campbell was
assigned to a hand crew along with two South Pasadena firefighters. The firefighters were
transported by helicopter in order to reach their assignment location. As a Fireline Paramedic,
Firefighter Campbell is responsible not only for his response as a firefighter, but also provides
medical assistance for any firefighters that are injured or require treatment.

On Saturday, August 15 Engine 91 and RA91, with assistance from the Alhambra, South
Pasadena, and San Gabriel Fire Departments, responded to a vegetation fire on the 1400 block
of St. Albans Road. Upon arrival, Engine 91 reported an Edison Pole was on fire with live wires
down, causing surrounding vegetation, palm trees, and an adjacent residence to catch fire. The
fire was confined to the roof of the residence, and adjacent vegitatation. Edison was contacted
for utility repair.

  2

  3-2  AGENDA ITEM 3
 On Monday, August 17 Firefighter/Paramedic Tannehill was dispatched as a Fireline Paramedic
(FEMP) to the Lake Fire in Castaic, CA where he remained on assignment for 15 days. As a FEMP
Trainee, Firefighter Tannehill is responsible for the rescue and medical care of fireline crews.
This assignment is very arduous as he is embedded with firefighting crews on the fireline.

On Saturday, August 29 Engineer White and Probationary Firefighter/Paramedic Dorsey were
dispatched as part of a relief crew for Strike Team 1204A at the SCU-Lightning Complex in Santa
Clara County, CA. The Strike Team was demobilized on Tuesday, September 1 and all personnel
returned to the station.

On Monday, September 7 Engine 91 was dispatched as part of a strike team to the Bobcat
Incident in the Angeles National Forest. Engine 91 is currently assigned to structure protection
and triage efforts within the foothill communities, and are actively patrolling neighborhoods and
preparing in the event that evacuation warnings are issued. As of September 10, 2020 the Bobcat
Incident had grown to approximately 23,890 acres and was 0% contained.

ARSON INVESTIGATIONS

San Marino Fire Investigators are currently investigating two fires that occurred in the Cities of
San Gabriel and Pasadena. Investigators are expected to make an announcement as to the cause
and origin of the San Gabriel Mission Fire within the next two weeks. The fatality fire that
occurred in Pasadena resulted in criminal charges being filed on Monday, August 31.

FY 2020-21 DEPARTMENT OBJECTIVES

  •  Complete a multi-year review of the City of San Marino’s Very High Fire Severity Zone
  to determine if the designated area in Chapter 14, Article 13 of the San Marino City Code
  remains suitable.
  •  Conduct a review of the current Community Emergency Response Training (CERT) and
  develop a “Citizen Fire Academy” for residents’ participation.
  •  Upgrade and improve the Emergency Operations Center.
  •  Conduct a City-wide emergency operations exercise with City staff, Department Heads,
  and the School District.
  •  Review and revise the City’s Emergency Operations Plan for City Council adoption.

FROM:  M. D. Rueda, Fire Chief

SUBJECT:  FIRE DEPARTMENT MONTHLY PERFORMANCE REPORT

The attached San Marino Fire Department July 2020 Performance Report represents the incident
data reports intended to meet the Improvement Goals referenced in the March 2, 2018 Report
to City Council titled; Implementation Plan Fire Department Deployment Study. The Fire
Department has been working closely with Verdugo Fire Dispatch (VFD) to ensure the accuracy
of the data being reported. Some of the data sets are not currently available from VFD and are
listed as N/A. VFD has been made aware of the San Marino Fire Department’s interest in pursuing
the data associated with the fire and life safety goals as approved by the City Council.

Improvement Goal A in the Report recommended the following:

Call Processing Goals

9-1-1 calls will be answered at the primary PSAP (Public Safety Answering Point) San Marino
Police Department within 15 seconds, 95% of the time.

9-1-1 calls will be transferred from the primary PSAP to Verdugo Fire Dispatch within 30 seconds
from the time answered, 95% of the time.

This data is not available.

Recommended Turnout Goal

Response personnel shall initiate the response of a unit capable of mitigating an incident to a
priority fire and rescue incident 80 seconds from notification 90% of the time.

Response personnel shall initiate response to all other priority incidents within 60 seconds from
notification 90% of the time.

Recommended First-Due Response Time Goal

The first response unit capable of initiating effective incident intervention shall arrive at a priority
fire or rescue incident within 5 minutes and 20 seconds from notification of response personnel,
90 percent of the time.

  3-4  AGENDA ITEM 3
 The first response unit capable of initiating effective incident intervention shall arrive at all other
priority incidents within 5 minutes from notification of response personnel, 90% of the time.

Recommended Response Force Goal

The full effective response force shall arrive at a moderate risk structure fire within 9 minutes
and 20 seconds of notification of response personnel, 90% of the time.

This data is not available.

Cardiac Arrest Data

The Cardiac Arrest data set includes the total number of cardiac arrest patients treated by
Firefighter/Paramedics. We always pray that the number is as low as possible. The more
important data sets are the subsequent measures which include the number of times the
Firefighter/Paramedics are successful in returning a patient’s spontaneous circulation (ROSC) –
our goal with ROSC is always 100%. Saving lives is why the Fire Department exists; unfortunately,
this is not always in our control. Lastly, the subsequent data sets measure the percentages of
correct treatments performed by the Firefighter/Paramedics.

Verdugo COVID-19 Response

Beginning in March 2020, Verdugo implemented increased screening measures and dispatch codes
for COVID-19 patients. Verdugo now dispatches potential COVID-19 patients as a SICK2
response. This alerts Fire Department Paramedics to potential coronavirus infection, and triggers
the protocol for the use of additional personal protective equipment (PPE). Dispatchers have
been trained to ask a series of questions to identify potential COVID patients. The screening
tool has increased the safety of responding personnel; however, it has also contributed to the
increase in the time to process these 911 calls.

SUBJECT:  REQUEST FOR EXEMPTION OF THE FORMAT OF PUBLIC
  SAFETY COMMISSION MINUTES

BACKGROUND

The City Clerk and staff prepare minutes for all City Council and City advisory body meetings,
including meetings of the Public Safety Commission (PSC). The minutes are the official record
of the meeting and reflect the type of meeting, when and where the meeting was held,
beginning and ending times, officials present, issues that were discussed, action taken, and how
members voted.

There are three basic types of formats for minutes, action, summary, and verbatim. Action
minutes reflect the action taken, including the maker and second of motions, and the vote of
each motion. The content of presentations and discussions are not included in action minutes.
Summary minutes include the information in action minutes plus a summary of points discussed
and individuals’ comments. Verbatim minutes are a “word by word” transcript of the
proceedings. A majority of California cities prepare action minutes, including the City of San
Marino.

DISCUSSION

On September 8, 2020, during a discussion with the Chair, it was requested that at the next
Public Safety Commission meeting a discussion of agenda minutes formatting be placed on the
Agenda for the September 14, 2020.

On average, the time to prepare summary minutes will take twice as much time to complete
compared to action minutes. A transition to action minutes has been found to streamline the
minute-making process and allows for a more efficient use of staff time. Thus, the San Marino
City Council voted to move to the action minute format on April 9, 2014, which impacted City

  6-1  AGENDA ITEM 6
 Council and advisory body records. A change to summary minutes would increase the time to
complete minutes to approximately 20 hours. This will have an operational effect on the Fire
or Police Staff as it relates to currently assigned duties.

Each meeting of the PSC is recorded and is available online to the public through the City
Website, https://www.cityofsanmarino.org/government/agendas___minutes_/2020.php. If a
member of the PSC or the public would need additional information it can be accessed for their
use.

FISCAL IMPACT

None

RECOMMENDATION

Staff recommends that the PSC continue to complete agenda minutes in action minute format
due to the increase in staff time to complete and review minutes for the PSC. Or, if the PSC
seeks the adoption of a revised format for PSC meeting minutes they may direct staff to take
the request to the City to seek an exemption. If the PSC concurs with staff’s recommendation
there will be no further action. If the PSC requests a change in format an appropriate motion
would be:

“I move to adopt the Summary Format for Public Safety Commission Minutes, upon
confirmation from the City Council; and direct staff to seek from the City Council an
exemption for the format of minutes for the PSC.”

SUBJECT:  PURCHASE OF RESCUE AMBULANCE TO REPLACE RESERVE
  RESCUE AMBULANCE 791

BACKGROUND

Emergency medical services (EMS) represent an integral public service provided by the San
Marino Fire Department (SMFD). In 2019, SMFD responded to 1,419 EMS incidents, or 74% of
all incidents. The Fire Department maintains a reserve rescue ambulance (RA) that is used as a
backup RA when the front-line unit is placed out of service for maintenance, repair, and is also
staffed by off-duty crews to provide supplemental resources and coverage in the event of a
disaster, hazardous weather, and for special events.

Vehicle Replacement Criteria
To ensure dependability in responding to EMS incidents, the SMFD maintains a replacement cycle
for an RA of twelve years. The current reserve RA was purchased in 2008 and is currently 12
years old. Following an annual review of the SMFD’s fleet, staff has determined that the reserve
RA has either met or exceeded its established replacement criteria. During the Fire Department
Annual Inspection, Fire Department and Public Works Department personnel discovered a
significant oil leak at the rear main seal. The vehicle requires updated equipment and space is
limited for equipment and staff. In the 2020 Fleet Utilization Study prepared by Management
Partners, it was recommended that the reserve ambulance be replaced during the 2020-2021
Fiscal Year.

The Fire Department assembled an RA specifications development committee in 2019 in
anticipation of the approval to purchase a new RA. Captain Dominic Petta led the committee
through a review of previous specifications from past SMFD purchases, recent specifications from
area fire departments that have made RA purchases, and lastly reviewed industry developments
in the ambulance industry. The committee developed specifications that were then sent out to
vendors utilized by several Southern California fire departments for the construction of RA’s.

  7-1  AGENDA ITEM 7
 The committee requested bids for a Type 1 custom build ambulance on a Dodge 5500, 5 x 2,
diesel powered two door standard cab chassis. As each RA is a custom build, cooperative
purchasing was not available as a consideration, and lease financing was unavailable with any of
the vendors that provided bids.

Each bid provided by the vendors met current State of California Code of Regulations Ambulance
safety standards (13 CCR § 1103; 13 CCR § 1103.2), Los Angeles County Code of Ordinances:
Ambulance – Design Requirements (LACC § 7.16.210); and Area C fire department industry
standards. The vehicle will also include the National Fire Protection Association minimum
standards as determined by the Fire Department’s RA specifications committee.

On June 26, 2020 the San Marino City Council approved the Fiscal Year 2020-2021 Budget. The
budget included $275,000 in capital improvement funds for the purchase of one Type 1 (cab
chassis with a modular ambulance body) RA vehicle to replace the 2008 vehicle currently assigned
as RA 791.

Republic EVS provided the lowest bid at $274,714.90 while meeting the SMFD RA specification.
Republic EVS currently has one remaining 2020 model cab chassis and would be able to begin
construction of the modular ambulance body immediately upon authorization from the SMFD.
Republic EVS is a Southern California based company located in Santa Fe Springs.

RECOMMENDATION

Staff recommends that the Public Safety Commission receive and file the report on the purchase
of a rescue ambulance to replace Rescue Ambulance 791.
